channel.title: Boca Libre Updates
channel.description: Secure, signed updates for Boca Libre.

item.description:
# Boca Libre 0.3.12
- Waits for a correction to finish before learning it, so multi-step edits such as “Radler” to “RadClerk” are saved in full. - Keeps the learning prompt at the capsule’s normal height and expands it smoothly to the right. - Gives you 15 seconds to reject a suggested vocabulary correction before it is added.

# Boca Libre 0.3.11
- Prevents the macOS alert sound that some browser text fields played when a dictation ended.

# Boca Libre 0.3.10
- Preserves the words around your cursor when inserting dictation in Google Docs, including one-letter words such as “a.” - Improves context-aware spacing, capitalization, and punctuation across Google Docs, Google Sheets, Claude, ChatGPT, and standard Mac text fields. - Prevents stray characters and truncated output in browser-based editors. - Prevents the macOS alert sound that some browser text fields played when a dictation ended. - Loads a saved OpenAI API key when Boca Libre starts, so pressing Right Option never interrupts dictation with a Keychain prompt. - Lets you switch between Apple on-device and OpenAI cloud transcription from the persistent capsule while it is idle. - Adds optional retake cleanup that keeps your corrected phrasing when you restate yourself.

# Boca Libre 0.3.9
- Shows a blue download control in the persistent dictation capsule when a new Boca Libre version is available. - Changes the download control to a clear “Update” label when you point at it. - Opens Boca Libre’s verified Sparkle update flow directly from the capsule. - Checks the signed public update feed daily even when automatic update alerts are turned off, without downloading or installing anything until you choose to update.

# Boca Libre 0.3.8
- Removes the rectangular window outline that could appear around the slender dictation capsule. - Uses the surrounding editor text more reliably when deciding capitalization at the cursor. - Keeps inserted phrases such as “for example” lowercase when they continue an existing sentence. - Preserves normal capitalization when dictation starts in a genuinely empty field.
